kept.title_or_quote: Ask HN: What do you want in a habit tracker?
kept.why_relevant: A thread collecting unmet needs in habit trackers, including frustration with streak-breaking mechanics.

rescore.why: The thread explicitly discusses streak freezes as essential to habit tracker retention, which is the core mechanic Streakly is built around.

kept.drafted_reply: The Duolingo streak-freeze comparison you raised is exactly the right frame — the research on this is pretty clear that all-or-nothing streaks optimize for guilt, not behavior change. A weekly-target model (did you hit 5 of 7 days?) tends to outperform daily chains for long-term adherence because it decouples one bad day from the entire motivation structure. Your flathabits.com already nails the privacy and no-account principles, so layering in a repair or forgiveness mechanic on top of what you have could meaningfully move your day-30 retention without touching the core simplicity. I built Streakly ({APP_URL}), which ships streak repair as its core mechanic rather than a paid add-on, if you want to see one implementation of this.
